newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commercial selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commercial selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on commercial selling, traders said.

"Cargill was the best seller of August with the Japanese buying early and at the close, Midland Walwyn bought May. Hedges pushed November down," a trader said. November WCE canola crush profit margins rose to -10.14 Thursday from -12.02 Wednesday.

Eastern Canadian crushers were rumored to be seeking European canola which was said to be C$30 a tonne cheaper while talk circulated that Mexico sourced two cargo loads of European seed as Canadian seed remained overpriced.
August canola fell $0.20 to $363, November down $1.70 to $343.90. November flax down $1.40 to $279.50 as commercials bought from hedgers. Sep-Nov at $6. Volume was 575 lots.
October western barley lost $0.50 to $126.50, December down $0.10 to $127.90 on commercial selling, UGG buying the lows. Volume was 200 lots.
October feed wheat rose $0.30 to $152.80, December down $0.30 to $152.80. Fifty Oct-Dec spread at even money. Volume was 500 lots.
Commission houses sold five December oats down US$0.60 to US$111.50 to commercials.
LFG bought October peas up US$0.50 to US$170. RBC-DS and UGG traded Oct-Dec at US$0.50. Volume was 27 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, feed peas).
